desc:
A directed graph has n nodes labelled 0 to n - 1. Each entry edges[i] = [a, b] is an edge from a to b. A topological order is an arrangement of all n nodes in a line such that, for every edge [a, b], node a comes before node b.

Count how many different topological orders the graph has, and return the count modulo 1,000,000,007. If the graph has a cycle (or a self-loop) there is no topological order and the answer is 0.

n = 3, edges = []                    -> 6
n = 3, edges = [[0,1],[0,2]]         -> 2
n = 4, edges = [[0,1],[1,2],[2,3]]   -> 1
n = 2, edges = [[0,1],[1,0]]         -> 0
constraints: 0 ≤ a, b < n; repeated edges, cycles and self-loops are allowed
hints: Listing all permutations is hopeless for n = 15, since 15! is more than a trillion. Many different permutations share the same set of nodes placed so far.
Let dp[mask] be the number of ways to arrange the nodes in mask as the first positions of a valid order. Which nodes can be placed next, given the set mask?

A node v outside the mask may be placed next if all of its predecessors are already in the mask: with pred[v] as a bitmask this is pred[v] & ~mask == 0. Then dp[mask | (1 << v)] += dp[mask]. The answer is dp[(1 << n) - 1].
editorial: The only thing that matters about the nodes already placed is which they are, not in what order, because the next node must simply have all its predecessors among them. That gives a DP over subsets: dp[mask] is the number of valid orders of the nodes in mask that can start a complete order.

Store for each node a bitmask pred[v] of its in-neighbours (repeated edges just set the same bit). Start with dp[0] = 1. For each mask in increasing numeric order (a mask is always smaller than the masks that add a bit to it), try each node v not in mask whose predecessors are all inside mask, and add dp[mask] to dp[mask | 1 << v], modulo 1,000,000,007.

The answer is dp of the full set. A self-loop makes a node its own predecessor, so it can never be placed and the full mask stays at 0; a longer cycle likewise blocks the DP, which gives the required 0 without a separate cycle check. The running time is O(2n * n) and memory O(2n). The count itself can reach 15!, so the modulo is needed.
